results.reason: Identifies the conflict between Schedule §1.1 (ship date) and MSA §1.3 (Rochester delivery). Explains that late delivery, risk and invoicing key off the ship date and that Harlow loses its transit-delay remedy.
Recommends conforming the Schedule's definition to the MSA (Rochester delivery) and adding an order-of-precedence clause under which the MSA controls.

Identifies that §4.3 covers all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7/US scope. Explains the blocking of other sourcing and non-US plants, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 in the US.

Identifies Verdane's one-sided assignment right under §15.2, including the competitor risk. Covers the risks to Specifications and to performance, and recommends Harlow's consent, a bar on assignment to competitors and a change-of-control termination right.

Identifies that Amendment §2 removes gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the carve-outs, leaving them subject to the 12-month fee cap. Recommends rejecting the change and keeping the original §11.2.
States the 12-month fees cap and the three original exclusions.
States that Term Sheet §3 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings in the United States and uses it as the baseline.
Notes New York law under §16.1, includes an assumptions section, and expressly cites no cases or statutes while flagging the need for verification.
Structured memo with a ranked issue list. Each issue gives location, why it matters and a fix, and there is an assumptions section.
Expressly treats the Term Sheet as evidence of the deal only, and lists the term and payment provisions as non-issues.
Section references appear accurate and party benefit is correctly stated. No fabricated authority.
